sourceRefs: Cicero, De Officiis III.77 (the proverb about micatio and honesty in the dark)
Parlett, David, The Oxford History of Board Games (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1999)

entries.name: Hopscotch
entries.period: recorded in English sources from the 17th century
sourceRefs: Gomme, Alice Bertha, The Traditional Games of England, Scotland, and Ireland (London: David Nutt, 1894–98)
Opie, Iona & Peter, Children's Games in Street and Playground (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1969)

entries.name: Jianzi
entries.period: documented from at least the Han period; still played
sourceRefs: Culin, Stewart, Korean Games, with Notes on the Corresponding Games of China and Japan (Philadelphia, 1895)
Bell, R. C., Board and Table Games from Many Civilizations (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1960–69)

entries.name: Marbles
entries.period: clay and stone marbles are ancient; the modern ring game is documented from the 17th century
sourceRefs: Opie, Iona & Peter, Children's Games in Street and Playground (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1969)
Gomme, Alice Bertha, The Traditional Games of England, Scotland, and Ireland (London: David Nutt, 1894–98)

entries.name: Conkers
entries.period: first recorded in the 1840s; a snail-shell antecedent is documented earlier
sourceRefs: Opie, Iona & Peter, Children's Games in Street and Playground (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1969)
Gomme, Alice Bertha, The Traditional Games of England, Scotland, and Ireland (London: David Nutt, 1894–98)

entries.name: Gonggi
entries.period: documented in the 1890s; still played
sourceRefs: Culin, Stewart, Korean Games, with Notes on the Corresponding Games of China and Japan (Philadelphia, 1895)
Opie, Iona & Peter, Children's Games in Street and Playground (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1969)

entries.name: Jan-ken
entries.period: the three-way hand game is documented in Japan from the 17th–19th centuries; it spread worldwide in the 20th
sourceRefs: Linhart, Sepp, 'Rituality in the Ken Game', in van Bremen & Martinez (eds.), Ceremony and Ritual in Japan (London: Routledge, 1995)
Culin, Stewart, Korean Games, with Notes on the Corresponding Games of China and Japan (Philadelphia, 1895)

entries.name: Cat's Cradle
entries.period: recorded in English sources from the 18th century; string figures are far older and near-universal
sourceRefs: Jayne, Caroline Furness, String Figures: A Study of Cat's-Cradle in Many Lands (New York: Scribner, 1906)
Haddon, Kathleen, Cat's Cradles from Many Lands (London: Longmans, 1911)

entries.name: Fivestones
entries.period: recorded in 19th-century collections; the skill form is far older
sourceRefs: Gomme, Alice Bertha, The Traditional Games of England, Scotland, and Ireland (London: David Nutt, 1894–98)
Opie, Iona & Peter, Children's Games in Street and Playground (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1969)

entries.name: Myinda
entries.period: named by Pollux in the 2nd century CE
sourceRefs: Pollux, Onomasticon IX (list and description of Greek games)
Gomme, Alice Bertha, The Traditional Games of England, Scotland, and Ireland (London: David Nutt, 1894–98) — the English cognate

entries.name: Ampe
entries.period: documented in 20th-century collections; widely played in schoolyards
sourceRefs: Zaslavsky, Claudia, Africa Counts: Number and Pattern in African Culture (Boston: Prindle, Weber & Schmidt, 1973)

entries.name: Mbube Mbube
entries.period: documented in 20th-century collections of southern African children's games
sourceRefs: Zaslavsky, Claudia, Africa Counts: Number and Pattern in African Culture (Boston: Prindle, Weber & Schmidt, 1973)

entries.name: Gilli-danda
entries.period: documented in 19th-century collections; cognate forms across Eurasia
sourceRefs: Gomme, Alice Bertha, The Traditional Games of England, Scotland, and Ireland (London: David Nutt, 1894–98) — the English 'tipcat' cognate
Bell, R. C., Board and Table Games from Many Civilizations (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1960–69)

entries.name: Pilolo
entries.period: documented in 20th-century collections of Ghanaian children's games
sourceRefs: Zaslavsky, Claudia, Africa Counts: Number and Pattern in African Culture (Boston: Prindle, Weber & Schmidt, 1973)

entries.name: Pétanque
entries.period: the modern form was fixed in 1907; the boules family is far older
sourceRefs: Parlett, David, The Oxford History of Board Games (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1999)
Fédération Internationale de Pétanque et Jeu Provençal, published rules of play
